title: Presbytery authority to conduct regular visitation of congregations
snippet: The CCB advised that BCO 13-9 grants presbytery the prerogative to initiate regular visitation of its churches for their spiritual welfare.

title: Teaching elder voting rights and congregational approval of pastoral salary changes
snippet: The CCB advised that a teaching elder votes as a full session member, and that any change to pastoral salary terms requires congregational approval as part of the call.

title: Whether congregation may dissolve the session by vote
snippet: A congregation cannot dissolve the session; it may by majority vote request individual officer removals under BCO 24-6, but the final decision rests with the session, and presbytery may assume jurisdiction under BCO 13-9.

title: Mandatory review of all previously unreviewed session minutes
snippet: The CCB advised that it is mandatory for a presbytery to review all previously unreviewed session records, not merely resume with current ones.

title: Erasure of a teaching elder seeking transfer to independent church
snippet: A presbytery wishing to release a minister to an independent church should handle it by erasure under BCO 38-3, which does not affect his ordination unless the church is heretical.

title: Language in which session records may be written and submitted
snippet: CCB advised that a presbytery may permit session records kept or translated into English when submitted, provided they meet BCO standards.

title: Eligibility of expired-term trustee to fill another trustee's unexpired term
snippet: The CCB advised that BCO 14-1-12 permits such a nomination only if the agency's assembly-approved bylaws explicitly authorize it.

title: Trustee with expired term filling another's unexpired vacancy
snippet: The CCB reaffirmed that BCO 14-1-12 permits an expired-term trustee to fill an unexpired vacancy only if agency bylaws approved by the Assembly specifically allow it.

title: Which GA entities are subject to the permanent committee ineligibility rule
snippet: The CCB clarified that the "permanent committee" ineligibility provision in RAO 13-2 applies only to the four committees enumerated in RAO 4-2, not to other GA entities.

title: SJC member eligibility for concurrent GA agency board service
snippet: The CCB advised that a member of the GA's Standing Judicial Commission is eligible to serve concurrently on the board of a General Assembly agency.

title: Consecutive service on different GA committees without sabbatical
disposition: No (not eligible); Adopted by the CCB
snippet: The CCB advised that a GA permanent committee member who completed a full term is not eligible for consecutive service on a different committee or agency board without a sabbatical year.

title: General Assembly committee authority over cooperative mission agreements
snippet: The CCB advised that the Committee of Commissioners channels business to the floor rather than acting as a commission, and the full Assembly retains authority over cooperative agreements.

title: Administrative Committee acting as an unlimited commission under Standing Rule 16
snippet: The CCB advised that Standing Rule 16 effectively created an unlimited commission contrary to BCO 15-1, which restricts commissions to specifically defined matters.

title: Referent of 'it' in BCO 15-1 regarding commission records
disposition: advice given — 'it' refers to concluding actions of the commission
snippet: The CCB concluded that 'it' in BCO 15-1 line 6 refers to the concluding actions of the commission, not the full record of proceedings, consistent with BCO 15-3's requirement that the commission's judgment be entered as the presbytery's action.

title: SJC authority to adjudicate issues not referred to it
disposition: advice given — SJC cannot adjudicate issues not referred to it
snippet: The CCB opined that the Standing Judicial Commission may not adjudicate any issue or matter not referred to it, as initiating new issues would improperly make the SJC a court of original jurisdiction.

title: Alternate commission member serving as chairman or voting when not needed for quorum
disposition: advice given — no constitutional prohibition on alternate serving as chairman or voting
snippet: The CCB found no constitutional prohibition on an alternate member serving as commission chairman, and ruled that an alternate filling a principal's vacancy may vote even when not needed to constitute a quorum.

title: SJC member eligibility for concurrent GA agency board service
snippet: The CCB advised that a member of the GA's Standing Judicial Commission is eligible to serve concurrently on the board of a General Assembly agency.

title: Administrative Committee acting as an unlimited commission under Standing Rule 16
snippet: The CCB advised that Standing Rule 16 effectively created an unlimited commission contrary to BCO 15-1, which restricts commissions to specifically defined matters.

title: Proper limits on presbyterial use of the extraordinary clause
snippet: The GA counseled that use of BCO 21-4's extraordinary clause must be limited to truly extraordinary circumstances or proven extraordinary gifts, warning against increasing laxity in application.

title: Proper limits on presbyterial use of the extraordinary clause
snippet: The GA counseled that use of BCO 21-4's extraordinary clause must be limited to truly extraordinary circumstances or proven extraordinary gifts, warning against increasing laxity in application.

title: Applicability of extraordinary clause to ministers from other denominations
snippet: The CCB advised that neither BCO 13-6 nor BCO 21-4 contains an extraordinary clause applicable to ministers transferring from other denominations.

title: Legality of dividing presbytery into sections to hear candidate sermons
snippet: The full presbytery must conduct all trial parts; dividing into sections to hear candidate sermons for ordination is impermissible except as a commission and should be treated as exceptional.

title: Legality of dividing presbytery into sections to hear candidate sermons
snippet: The full presbytery must conduct all trial parts; dividing into sections to hear candidate sermons for ordination is impermissible except as a commission and should be treated as exceptional.

title: Dividing presbytery into parts to hear ordination candidate sermons
snippet: BCO 21-4 does not permit presbyteries to divide simply into committees to hear ordination sermons; division into commissions is not prohibited but should be exceptional, not regular practice.

title: Scope of the extraordinary clause for ordination candidates
snippet: The CCB advised that under BCO 18-2 the extraordinary clause excuses only the six-month membership period, not the session endorsement, the two-month filing deadline, or the one-year internship sequence.

title: Extraordinary clause exemptions from licensure examinations
snippet: In extraordinary cases a presbytery may exempt a candidate from any of the prescribed parts of the licensure examination under BCO 19-2, though the clause must not be used as a subterfuge to avoid historic training requirements.

title: Scope of extraordinary clause relative to educational prerequisites
snippet: BCO 21-4's extraordinary clause applies only to listed trial parts for ordination, not to prerequisite requirements such as college diploma, seminary diploma, and internship completion.

title: Re-examination of previously ordained officer nominees by session
disposition: advice given — re-examination required; session may find nominee deficient
snippet: The CCB advised that all nominees for ruling elder or deacon, including previously ordained individuals, must be re-examined by the session, which retains the right to find them deficient.

title: CRPR authority to review presbytery granting of ordination exceptions
snippet: The CCB advised that a presbytery's granting of exceptions under BCO 21-4 is reviewable by the Committee on Review of Presbytery Records, which must report apparent violations accordingly.

title: Use of translations and translators in presbytery ordination examinations
snippet: Whether translations and translators may be used in presbytery examinations is left to the presbytery's judgment as to whether qualifications are fully satisfied.

title: Presbytery discretion in granting exceptions to BCO stated differences
snippet: The CCB advised that a presbytery may ask candidates to state differences with the BCO but is not required to do so, and the BCO provides no mechanism for formally recognizing such differences.

title: Recording candidate's views on male-only eldership at ordination
snippet: No constitutional procedure exists to record a candidate's views on the BCO's requirements, nor is a candidate required to list his differences with its provisions.

title: Ordination of men who believe women may serve as deacons
snippet: Believing Scripture permits women deacons, while agreeing to abide by BCO standards in practice, is not by itself sufficient grounds to deny ordination or reception in the PCA.

title: Propriety of abstractly listing disqualifying beliefs for ordination
snippet: The GA declined to determine abstractly which beliefs disqualify a man from office, holding that only proper judicial processes may make such binding determinations.

title: Handling exceptions at ordination and distinctions between BCO and confessional exceptions
snippet: Courts must investigate stated exceptions; BCO exceptions under vow 3 are handled differently from doctrinal exceptions under vow 2, with judicial process available if warranted.

title: Liberty granted by exceptions versus right to teach contrary to standards
snippet: Ordination with exceptions grants personal liberty to hold minority views but does not warrant public teaching or preaching of those views in ways that disturb the church's peace and purity.

title: Call of assistant pastor from another denomination without presbyterial examination
snippet: A session may not call an ordained assistant pastor from another denomination without presbytery approval and examination, as all teaching elders must be members of the serving presbytery.

title: Pastoral oversight and discipline when spouses are in different jurisdictions
snippet: CCB advised that no constitutional obstacle prevents courts from different presbyteries cooperating in marital reconciliation, though the BCO makes no provision for joint commissions of separate courts.

title: Rotating sessions, ballot control, and officer election procedures
snippet: The CCB answered five questions on officer elections: the session must present all eligible men, the congregation determines the number elected, and no constitutional limit restricts election frequency beyond a 30-day notice.

title: Session limiting eligible nominees on officer election ballot
snippet: A session may not withhold qualified nominees from the congregation's ballot to limit board size; BCO 24-1 requires all eligible men to be reported to the congregation.

title: Session authority over officer nominees and inactive elders under rotation
snippet: A session must present all qualified nominees for election and may not use BCO 24-6 to exclude inactive officers; presbytery proceedings are not automatically required for long-inactive elders.

title: Re-examination and divestiture of officers in rotational systems
snippet: The CCB advised that the BCO provides no procedure for re-examining rotated-off officers' qualifications, but divestiture may only occur under BCO 24-6, 38-2, or 34-10.

title: Re-examination of previously ordained officer nominees by session
disposition: advice given — re-examination required; session may find nominee deficient
snippet: The CCB advised that all nominees for ruling elder or deacon, including previously ordained individuals, must be re-examined by the session, which retains the right to find them deficient.

title: Setting a nomination deadline before the one-month officer election notice
disposition: advice given — session may set nomination deadline before one-month meeting notice; all six required elements must be included
snippet: A session may set a nomination deadline before the one-month congregational meeting notice expires, but all six BCO 24-1 requirements for officer election must be met.

title: Application of BCO 24-1 examination process to re-election of officers
snippet: BCO 24-1 applies fully to men with no prior official relationship to the church; for men already serving, lower courts determine which provisions apply at re-election.

title: Grounds and procedures for removing members from PCA church rolls
disposition: declined to answer specific questions; general advice given
snippet: Declining to address case-specific questions, the CCB outlined the three BCO provisions by which members may be removed from church rolls: transfer, discipline, or relocation.

title: Whether deletion from the roll under BCO 46-5 constitutes excommunication
snippet: The CCB answered yes — 'deletion' under BCO 46-5 is excommunication in effect, and the due-process procedures of BCO 27-5 must therefore be followed.

title: Procedure for removing members who relocate without affiliating elsewhere
snippet: BCO 46-2 governs removal of members who move away and fail to affiliate within a year; BCO 46-5's formal discipline applies only to willful neglect, not mere relocation.

title: Teaching elder voting rights and congregational approval of pastoral salary changes

title: Presbytery jurisdiction and restoration path for a deposed and repentant minister

title: Presbytery authority to remove censure of suspended or deposed teaching elder

snippet: BCO prohibitions on debate apply only to the specific matter complained, only until final adjudication, and to all members of the lower court — expiring upon final resolution.

title: Recourse when General Assembly may have erred in a decision

title: Proper use of memorials and finality of adjudicated GA decisions
snippet: A memorial under BCO 40-5 is the proper recourse for alleging GA error after adjournment; the Assembly will not reopen a finally adjudicated case except to correct a manifest error.

title: Review and control action while a judicial case is pending on appeal

title: Permissible scope of communion practice under BCO 58-4
snippet: The GA denied closed communion (members of the local congregation only) as incompatible with BCO 58-4, affirming open or close communion while requiring baptism as a prerequisite to the Table.

title: Ordination of candidate with exceptions to six-day creation and male-only office
snippet: New River Presbytery's response to prior exceptions was found satisfactory by the GA, though the Review Committee urged the presbytery not to approve future candidates whose exceptions deny fundamentals such as six-day creation or male-only ordination.
